items.notes: Very nice quality bootleg with Lindsay K Northen, who had been one of the Glinda understudies for years.

Amazing video from the orchestra from a great angle. Shaky when zooming in and out in the first 30 minutes, and a few heads in frame at times, but the filming is unmatched. This was supposed to be Jackie Burns’ last night, but she’d been sick since late January and ended up missing this performance. Donna is just INCREDIBLE as Elphaba… Master has released a new 2023 remaster that is available through him.

T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.
A copy of this video is circulating that crashes VLC 30 minutes into Act 2, it's unknown if this issue comes from the original release.
Excellent video

This is Kristin and Norbert's last show. It was also supposed to be Joel Grey's last show, but he was ill. Video is sound only for the first 4 minutes and for the last 30 seconds of Defying Gravity. This is a great video with excellent sound. Includes the speech by Idina. This bootleg is a treasure.
Multiple copies are circulating. The best is the 7.8 GB file, which has higher video resolution, working menus, and the playbill. The 7.63 GB file has the same video quality but no playbill, skips 1 minute in late Act 1 (A Sentimental Man (Reprise)), skips the first 1.5 minutes of Act 2, and the smalls may glitch such that the last section of Act 1 doesn't play at all. The 4.07 GB file has worse video quality but does have a working menu, and includes the playbill and various extras (TV spots, Macy's special, Seth's Broadway Chatterbox).
Excellent HD capture with no obstructions. Caroline is an extremely strong Elphaba.

Great performances from both Rachel and Ginna. Nicely captured with no obstruction, just a couple quick dropouts and some occasional washout. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
Halloween! Great performance from all the cast here. Includes a Broadway Cares/Equity Fights Aids speech by Aaron Tveit at the end. Wonderful quality, kind of shaky though
T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.

T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.

Last Chicago show

This is a wonderful cast and Erin does a terrific Glinda; her Popular is very cute and funny. Dee and Brad remain one of my favorite couples and give great performances. Wonderful quality, crystal clear picture and sound. A
Crystal clear picture and sound. First five minutes are shaky, due to settling in and latecomers. After that, amazing picture and closeups. A+

T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.

Beautiful capture with amazing closeups. Performances were fantastic all the way around. Teal is wonderful and Megan is at the top of her game. A+
This show is Eden, Adam and Carol's last performance.
Closing Night in Los Angeles. Audio only for the first 7 minutes. Video doesn't start until around the time Glinda sings “She died alone” in No One Mourns the Wicked.
Crystal clear picture and sound. AMAZING quality, one of the top Wicked's. Fantastic cast and includes the extended scenes. A+

Penultimate, final performance of Cèline Purcell and Ferry Doedens. Muck-up show. Awesome filming quality, very steady, with a perfect mix of zooms, close-ups and stageshots so that all the action is captured. One of the top Wickeds.
Katie's last performance.
This was supposed to be Patti Murin's last show as Glinda but she couldn't make it because she was ill. Cassie hits the optional high note in No One Mourns the Wicked. Image can be blurry at times.
Beautiful HD capture with no obstructions and clear sound; Emmy has an amazing voice.

items.venue: SAFE Credit Union Performing Arts Center
items.notes: A perfect capture of the current First National Tour with some understudies. Emmy is a phenomenal Elphaba with great acting choices and amazing riffs. Very interesting to see a Fiyero mid-show switch; Kyle jumps in to Act Two seamlessly. One of my best captures with no blackouts, no washout, no obstruction, and very steady filming. This is shot slightly wider than usual, particularly when the ensemble is on stage, so you can see a lot more of the action. There are still close-ups when necessary. As usual, it's filmed in 16:9, and the sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.

A fantastic capture of Jessica Vosks and Kristen Martins debut performance. The capture is filmed with new equipment and is very stable and smooth. Recorded from the front of the balcony, with minimal heads to work around. Fantastic mix of close ups, medium shots, and wides when necessary. Jessica is strong straight out of the box and has great chemistry with Amanda.
Filmed January 3 & 4, 2017 and aired on PBS on October 27, 2017.

With a mix of original cast and new faces, there are great performances all around. Nicely captured with just a couple quick dropouts. There are some heads at the bottom of the screen that regularly block the actors' feet, but they are worked around as much as possible, and generally don't affect the main action. There is also some occasional washout, especially in wider shots. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
Screenshots are from the 3.99 GB single disc version.

Filmed from the 4th row. Sometimes unfocuses from the action but there are great close-ups. No video of the flying scene, as the last 10 minutes of Act 1 are audio only. B
DVD circulates in multiple copies, the most common of which is 4.01 GB. These, however, have intense generation loss. The first generation DVD is 3.91 GB, and this is where the screenshots below come from.
Several versions circulate, some compressed and ripped. Check with traders.

Javier is fantastic in the lead role; he's very different from Lin—a bit darker, more intense, and less care-free, but just as passionate. The understudies are great as well, but Andrew is the stand-out; his nuanced performance as Philip is heartbreaking. Seeing the show with so many new faces proves that it has legs beyond the original cast and will continue to be a hit. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
This is the correct date for the low quality video labeled as June 16, 2016.
Available as both law quality 480p VOBs (with smalls) and HD 1080p MKVs (16.81 GB for Act 1, 17.08 GB for Act 2. 33.89 GB total).
Shot from mezzanine with no head obstructions so a very clear shot. A little a bit shaky for the first number but steady after. Opening night was on the 20th, so this is a very early performance.
Shoshana's second show as Elphaba

Great performance from Idina at the Halloween performance. Shot around a head, but worked around as well as possible. Has a few glitchy spots and missing the last three minutes. Some great vocals and riffs from Idina, not previously captured on video. B+

The original Broadway cast of Rent reunites for Rent 10, a one night-only, benefit concert version of the show to mark the 10th anniversary of Jonathan Larsons landmark musical. Includes intro speeches by Allan Gordon, Mayor Bloomberg, Senator Schumer. Beautifully shot, amazingly clear video. An enthusiastic audience and a few flubs by the cast makes this video even more fun. A

A wonderful capture of Jessica's final performance, with no obstructions or washout. Jessica gave a top-notch performance and added new riffs. There are a few quick dropouts during applause and a nice mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. Audio is perfect and curtain call is included. *Commonly mislabelled, the MP4 is Tornado With Pigtails' master from the same performance.
Jessica Vosk's final show.

Great capture of JV Elphaba! Starts during NOMTW, right before Glinda enters. Shot with two different cameras from the same angle, so the picture quality occasionally varies slightly. My HD camera ran out of battery during A Sentimental Man, so I switched right to my 720p camera for the rest of Act One and all of Act Two, minor shakiness and occasional washout, but overall the video quality is excellent.

About five minutes worth of cover-ups at the beginning (you see Glinda's entrance) because of latecomers and a few more random ones during the first Act. The first few minutes of the second Act are similar to those of Act One. No obstructions, and incredible close-ups. There are 1-disk and 2-disk versions of this video, so check before trading.
Final Broadway Performance for Eden Espinosa, one disc or two disc version available

Excellent HD capture of Jackie's return to the role, captured from the orchestra. Jackie remains one of the most powerful and brilliant Elphaba's of all time. Stunning riffs, growls and variations, a perfect performance! A+
Beautiful HD capture of the out-of-town tryout! Idina and the rest of the cast have beautiful performances and wonderful vocals. A
Beautiful HD capture with no obstructions. Has some variations from the Pre-Broadway version, including cut songs, added songs and scenes. This version seems more streamlined and a great piece. A

There are a couple quick dropouts during the prologue and What If?, and the first half of Act One is a bit shaky, but it's much better as the show goes on. There is one head that obstructs a small portion of the front of the stage, but it never blocks more than the actors' feet and it's rarely noticeable overall. There is no washout, and the sound is excellent as usual. It's filmed in 16:9 with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.

Quality: Act 1 is mostly complete minus a few black outs, cover ups due to late comers, its quite shakey at the start while trying to focus in on the zoom. A few heads in the way but shot around them very well. If you have the Jackie Burns u/s DVD its exactly the same quality only more of the show. First act is 1 hour 15+ minutes and Second Act minus Hey Kid is little over an hour. Excellent Audio.

Stunning HD capture of Jackie and Charles in the lead roles. Jackie gives a flawless and powerful performance, which was beautifully sung. Flawless capture with no obstructions! **BEWARE of copies where one of the VOB files has been replaced with a lower quality MP4**

Excellent HD capture of one of Jackie's final performances. Promo footage was being filmed this day and her parents were sitting right behind me. She held the final note in Starting Over for 19 seconds. Such a wonderful performance! A

items.venue: Denver Center for the Performing Arts - Buell Theatre
items.notes: Beautiful HD capture of the very first performance on tour. The cast was full of energy and really ready to perform the show, since the Broadway closing. I have never heard Idina sing the score as she had this night, with great new riffs, variations and such power. Nailed it!

Idina's last performance. An emotional performance by the whole cast, particularly Idina. Her feelings overcome her during Always Starting Over and the Finale, leading to roaring cheers of support from the crowd. There is also a fantastic blooper during What If: Elizabeth's phone rings and the phone is not in her pocket. Chaos ensues. A really fantastic capture with no obstruction, no washout, and just two quick dropouts in Act One. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans. A
Beautiful capture of the tour, which features three new cast members joining the tour for the leads. Jackie is such a powerhouse and driving force! A+
Beautiful HD capture of Betsy joining and Drew returning to the cast. Betsy remains one of my and Broadway's new unstoppable leading ladies, which is clearly stated in this role! A

Beautiful capture of this stunning Broadway transfer. This is the performance where the set broke and Sara Bareilles came out while it was being fixed. She sang a cut song from the show and Part of Your World and talked with the audience, which is included. A+

items.format: VOB (with smalls) - 4.27 GB; VOB (with smalls) - 7.45 GB; M2TS - 24.02 GB
items.notes: Filmed from the right orchestra, at a slight angle, but excellent quality. The taper originally released this as a blu-ray, 2-disc DVDs or 1-disc DVD, so make sure to get the version that best suits your needs.

Some head and railing obstructions throughout the show. Misses the far right side of the stage but some nice close-ups and excellent sound on the video. First couple minutes of each act are blacked out, and there are a few quick dropouts throughout the show. 2 disc. Sunsetblvd79s master is better than this copy, this one is just for completionists.
Some spotlight washout, but overall a nice video. A-.

Great to see Dee on Broadway finally. The real treat is Michelle's return to Nessarose. She gives a great, original and true performance as Nessa. Beautiful capture with lots of energy from the cast. A

Excellent capture of Jackie and Chandra before heading off to Broadway. Jackie really gives a great Elphaba and great variations from girls past. Chandra gives lots of energy and good times in Popular.

Final performance for Stephanie J. Block. Great capture of possibly the best performance ever given by an Elphaba. SJB lit the stage on fire, honestly this is one of the best individual performances I have ever attended. With such power and control, this is one Wicked NOT to be missed, you will be amazed! Kendra and SJB get emotional during For Good and it's a beautiful moment between them.

AMAZING capture, closeups, performances. Not to be missed. A+

Content warning, there is partial nudity in this bootleg.
Final performance for Aaron Tveit. No video until “So have another drink of green elixir” in No One Mourns The Wicked.
Excellent HD capture of the replacement cast members. The show is still in wonderful shape, with a terrific cast and stellar performances! A

Beautiful HD capture of the new cast change, as composer Sara Bareilles takes over Jenna. Her performance of What Baking Can Do will knock you onto the floor! Terrific and fresh cast with a ton of exciting energy! A
Actors Benefit Performance. Includes post-show speeches.

Beautiful capture of this amazing show. Terrific show with so much talent and wonderful fun songs. Stephanie continues to knock it out of the park, Megan is pure perfection and Allison's comedic timing is hilarious. There are no obstructions in this wonderful capture. A+

Act One only of the Broadway opening night; shot in 16:9 widescreen. Coverups during 9 to 5, the second half of I Just Might and the scene right before Backwoods Barbie and about a minute at the end of the dream sequences; camera also wanders sometimes and heads in the wide shots when taper zoomed out to get the whole picture; DVD includes Get Out and Stay Out from the April 17th performance with Gaelen Gilliland as Judy.Well-shot from the orchestra.There is sometimes the top of a head at the bottom of the screen, but it never blocks Gaelen.

Final performance! Filmed in 16:9 widescreen. Few obstructions, only in the wide-shots when there are two heads on either side of the frame, but filmer does his/her best to shoot around them. External audio fed into video from MD recorder, so audio is very clear. A mix of close-ups and wider shots when multiple people were on stage to see their interactions. This was a gut-wrenchingly sad performance. Most of the cast members were in tears at some point or another during the show. In particular, Stephanie was sobbing through I Just Might and Allison started sobbing at the end of One of the Boys. A few minor ad-libs and mishaps. One being when Allison pulled out a tape measure during the urinals bit of One of the Boys. The cast was sad but they were clearly trying to have the times of their lives and go out with a bang. And they fed off the audience energy, which was insane and very supportive.
Very nice capture of the two-night only concert. Recorded from the back of the Balcony, but everything is nicely captured!

Beautiful HD capture of this wonderful show. This show is so much fun and the cast is perfection! I really can not single out one person as I could rave about every single person. This is one of the best shows to come along in a while, flawless! Datchery: Helena, Murderer: Rosa, Lovers: Puffer & Crisparkle. A

Another beautiful HD capture of this fantastic show. The cast is even tighter since previews and this is such a fun show with a terrific cast that is perfection! Hilarious Lovers scene at the end with Puffer and Bazzard! Murderer: Rosa Bud, Datchery: Helena, Lovers: Puffer and Bazzard. A+

Excellent HD capture of the final show. The audience was full of fans of the show, so great energy and applause throughout. Includes the only time three lovers were selected, including John Jasper. Touching final curtain speech by the director and Rupert Holmes. Datchery: Bazzard, Murderer: Puffer, Lovers: Helena and Jasper and Rosa Bud. A

An absolutely stellar tour cast with fantastic performances all around. Some great nuanced interpretations of the characters make the show fresh. This capture is nearly perfect with just one dropout toward the end of My Shot that lasts less than a minute. There is one head that occasionally blocks the actors' legs on the right side of the stage. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
Caissie's first as Elphaba, and she tore it up and put it on a silver platter. Beautiful capture and vocals. Kendra is hilarious at this performance. A
Skips from the end of I'm Not That Girl/scene with Morrible straight into the beginning of Defying Gravity
Excellent HD video with clear picture and sound filmed from the center mezzanine.
Heads at the bottom of the screen during a good part of the show when action takes place at the foot of the stage, but it's shot around well. A-
Filmed from the back of the orchestra. There are times that a cloth that the master is using covers the lens. Bette gets a standing ovation after Hello Dolly and at curtain call.
Excellent quality, however a vertical post on the left gets in the way occasionally, but is well filmed-around. A great capture of Donna in the role. A-
Excellent HD capture of the new campy musical filled with 70s hits! The cast does a wonderful job with camp and really commits, which makes it a very fun show! A

Final Broadway Performance. Excellent HD capture of the final show. The audience was full of fans of the show, so great energy and applause throughout. Three lovers were selected, including John Jasper. Touching final curtain speech by the Director and Rupert Holmes.
Masters Release Notes: A+ I think this is a BEAUTIFUL video!!! No blackouts, no obstructions and always following the action closely. *Last few minutes are from 12/7/11

Well filmed from the balcony on the first night of previews. Occasional heads appear in the bottom of the shot. A bit shaky at times, but overall pretty good, with great close ups.
Multiple copies are circulating; the 4.38 GB file is the same as the 4.18 GB file, except with the menu file duplicated (in both VIDEO_TS.VOB and VTS_01_0.VOB).

A great capture of the American premiere at La Jolla Playhouse. The incredibly talented cast delivers the score beautifully. Michael and Ciara both give powerhouse performances. This is a perfect capture with no blackouts, no obstruction, and just slight washout in some wide shots. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans. Most copies currently circulating have a glitch in the smalls. The higher quality copy known to be circulating is the VOBs + Smalls version that is 7.51 GB.

Great HD capture of the much hyped Shakespeare in the Park Production. Beautifully thought out and executed production with a few flubs and bloopers that are hilarious. Donna and Amy were just sensational! A-. Complete file should have both title screens and chapter menus for each disc (8.06 GB).
Beautiful HD capture of Heather's return to the theater as The Witch. Heather brought her signature voice and acting chops to the stage. Great performances from everyone at the famous outdoor venue!

Multiple versions circulating; the correct one, 8.20 GB, should include a Disc 2 title screen and two chapter menus, with the end of Act 1 on VTS_01_1.VOB and Act 2 starting on VTS_02_1.VOB.
A lower quality MP4/MOV rip (1.8 GB) circulates as May 6, 2014.

items.show: Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812
items.notes:
Nice HD capture of this immersive production that takes place all over the theater. Everything is captured as well as can be done in this setting. A beautiful production with so many layers and phenomenal performances. A-

Contains the song Natasha Lost before it was cut.

items.show: Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812
items.notes: Beautiful HD capture from the orchestra of Oak and Ingrid's final performances. Hands down the best capture of this show and from the perfect angle. All drama aside, Oak gave a rousing performance. A

items.show: Sunday in the Park with George
items.notes: Excellent HD capture of the Broadway transfer. The performances have really been fine tuned and beautifully performed. Jake and Annaleigh are perfection together. A
Archival recording. Stunning touring production with a massive cast, fabulous set and costumes. Mostly close up and medium shots but theres a few amazing wide shots.

Multi-Cam Pro-shot, in English. Says For preview purposes only. Not for commercial use during the entire video at the bottom of the screen. 2 versions floating around.  A complete version, normally at a higher video quality.  Also an incomplete version, the last 10 minutes substituted from the January 3, 2001 Broadway video.  Screenshots to compare.

Theres a little obstruction and generation loss, no close ups, but overall, a good capture of this beloved revival. Two versions of this disc exists. One with a timestamp and also includes Commerical, E! on Broadway segment, and 30 minute Carousel opening night special. The second has with no timestamp, and the only bonus feature is about 12 minutes of professionally shot footage. Ask your trader which version you have. Screenshots are of the copy without a timestamp.

Excellent HD capture of the new revival which been stripped down and streamlined to focus on Celie's journey. Some beautiful moments in the show with the direction and simplicity spotlighting the story. A few blackouts in the first 5 minutes, as clueless ushers fumbled around. A

30th Anniversary Gala. Includes only the last 30 minutes, the Special Finale with Cameron Mackintosh, Claude-Michel Schönberg, Alain Boublil, Herbert Kretzmer, John Owen-Jones, Gerónimo Rauch, and the original 1985 cast: Colm Wilkinson, Patti LuPone, Frances Ruffelle, Roger Allam. Featuring the Wales Millennium Kids Choir.
Eden Espinosa's first performance as Elphaba.
Closing night in Toronto! Shoshanas final show, as well as Megan and K Todd Freemans last on tour. Megan hits the opt-up at the end of Thank Goodness.
Eden, Carol and Adams final performance.

items.venue: Hobby Center For The Performing Arts
items.notes: Jackies first performance as Elphaba.

Excellent HD capture of Brandy Norwood joining the cast as Roxie. Everything is nicely captured, though a few minor and quick parts to the extreme far right can be blocked a few times. Brandy did an excellent job in the role and was really giving a solid performance! A-

Great HD capture of the final Broadway cast. Filmed just 2 days before the show closed. Keke is great as Ella but a very different voice from Laura and Paige. One slight head at the bottom at times but very visible. No washouts.

Filmed from the back of the balcony. Many heads appear in the frame to start, then when the filmer gets his bearings, the video improves greatly. There are a few times (mostly at the beginning) when the filmer replaces some poor video moments with still shots.  These still shots are less than 2 or 3 minutes of the entire show.  Overall, a great video, and Megan Hilty is amazing

A fantastic capture of this lavish production. It's refreshing to see different faces in the lead roles, and both Nathaniel and Earl carry the show well. Nathaniel's vocals are powerful and he has a great rapport with Caissie and Samantha. A lovely capture overall with no obstruction. Look Down is mostly blacked out and there are a couple quick dropouts during The Bishop scene and Lovely Ladies, but the show is otherwise fully intact. There is also some washout in high-contrast wide shots. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
First preview on Broadway.
Lots of obstruction from railings and the audience. It can be pretty shakey at times and some things are obstructed, but it gets better as show goes on. B

Haven did a splendid job as Fiona, bringing a lot of energy and great vocals to the table. It was interesting to see Mama Bear also be Gingy, since they were short on cast members. Beautiful clear capture with no obstructions.
Excellent HD capture of this hilarious new musical. The cast is just too perfect in every way. Superb performances, music, and story, and a great homage to theatre and musicals. Not to be missed! A
The best filming of Wicked ever! Shot close to the stage, with tons of closeups. Amazing quality. A+

First five minutes of each act are shaky with cover-ups (I've never seen so many latecomers at a show), and there are also blackouts after some songs in Act One. Incredible close-ups; you can see tears in Eden's eyes during her heart-wrenching “I'm Not that Girl.” Audience is electric, a satisfying show overall. Gaelen, in her early 20s, brings an interesting take to Morrible's role, as probably the youngest actress to play her.

This all-star cast gives energetic and nuanced performances; the cast as a whole is a stand-out with absolutely incredible dance numbers. Nicely filmed with no obstructions, no washout, just a couple of quick dropouts. Filmed the stage directly; screens are never shown. Filmed in 16:9 with a mix of wides, mediums and close-ups. Show is 125 minutes on one disc. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
Great HD capture, a week before the closing performance. First 10 or so minutes are full stage shot, then zooming begins. Still a great cast with some great songs and moments in the show. A-

This show is magical, Phillipa is captivating, and the entire ensemble is perfectly quirky. There have been a few changes since Berkeley that tighten up the show a bit and make it ready for Broadway. A near perfect capture with no washout, no obstruction, and just one very quick dropout. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.

A little jump now and then. Some cover ups at the end of songs; first 30 seconds of sound is very high. A tiny bit of minor clipping but great picture and sound throughout of the closing show. Two videos exist from the closing show. Some have Pigerty and Julie's swapped/mislabeled- check the screenshots.

T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.

Stephanie makes a remarkable Reno with such a voice and quite different from Sutton. Everything is nicely captured here and includes the new replacements Erin and Jessica. The last four minutes, which is the end of the wedding, are audio only. A

This concert version of the show is abridged with shortened scenes, simple costumes, and no sets or choreography, but Jeremy, Solea, and Karen are absolutely phenomenal with soaring vocals and emotional performances. Very well captured with no dropouts, no obstruction, and no washout. The stage is filmed directly most of the time; the screens are occasionally filmed, usually when the actors are not onstage. It's filmed in 16:9, with a mix of wides, mediums, and close-ups. The sound is excellent. Includes curtain call and playbill scans.
Great clear capture with no washout. One quick dropout in the first few minutes of Act One, and a railing that can be seen occasionally but never affects the action.
Beautiful HD capture of the Revival following opening night. Such a talented cast and the chemistry amongst them is incredible. Beautifully executed and not to be missed! A
Excellent HD capture of the first preview performance! This is the Pre-Broadway premiere of the Nickelodeon musical based on the TV show! Fun show and music with no obstructions! A+

Shoshana, David, Rue and Michelle's last performance. The whole cast was really having fun, very high audience energy throughout. Megan and Shoshana have a really funny bit during Popular, and the crowd went wild. Camera wanders quite a bit and is shaky at points due to the blind filming, plus some spotlight washout. Still, this recording is an absolute gem. Includes Playbill scans and Megan's post-show speech.
T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.

HD capture of the final Pre-Broadway performance. A drunk woman's head blocks most of the left side and she does not sit still. This is far from perfect, but if you want a glimpse in the Moulin Rouge... the show is sensational! B

Excellent HD capture of the new production by Studio Tenn & TPAC. This was a huge show with a very large cast. Some terrific staging moments and of course Eden did a fantastic job as Eva. Beautiful production! A

T/W: This video contains a PETA advertisement at the beginning, which contains graphic images and may be distressing.  This was included by the master on release.

Excellent capture of the stunning and much talked about Chicago production. Superb performances from the entire cast and beautiful to watch! A
Kristin is on Vicodin because of her neck injury. She messes up lyrics in NOMTW, but hits the optional High Note in NOMTW & Thank Goodness.
Directed by Michael Arden. Opening night.
Annaleighs last performance. Includes Stephanie J Blocks speech

Megan Hilty's last show in the Broadway run (she will reprise the role of Glinda in the Los Angeles run).
A very Megan-centric recording, good close-ups and follows the action very well. Includes detailed scene selection, playbill scans at the start (DVD 1) and stage door recordings (DVD 2). One of, if not the best performance of Megan.
Really nice capture of Jordin Sparks performance as Nina. Only one or two coverups that last for under three seconds each.
Some spotlight washout, not too bad
Excellent HD capture of 2018 Tony winner for Best Revival. Sensational show and cast, not to be missed! A-
Becca Petersen was on for Caitlyn Caussin (Swung in)
First Preview! The flower gets caught in Kristin's wig during Popular, which leads to lots of ad-libbing. Norbert calls out a ringing cell phone during the lion cub scene.

Excellent capture with many great close ups. Shot at a 2 pm show by Major. A

Act 1 only. First recorded no-fly show.
filmed with two cameras
Wonderful fresh new cast. Dee and Brad add great new vocals, and Megan was a terrific Glinda. Watch for funny blooper in Popular. Amazing quality, one of the top Wicked's out there. A+

Lisa, Annaleigh & Kris' first performance in the company. Annaleigh sings the optional high note in No One Mourns the Wicked, and I think this is the only time this was captured (especially because she almost never did that). Overall AMAZING performance and chemistry. The acting and singing could not have been any better. Lisa was in top-notch form. Annaleigh was beyond quixotic and the rest of the cast was just on fire. A+

items.notes: This is the only publicly released video recording of this acclaimed, sold out production with the original West End revival cast. This was my first time recording and as a result, mistakes were made. Foolishly, I set the exposure to automatic, so the recording suffered from spotlight washout (I haven't made this mistake since). The washout has mostly been fixed in editing but it's impossible to fully correct. The recording has more zooms than I would like, to prevent further washout. Fortunately, this production is minimalistic and performance-focused so it doesn't hinder the overall experience of the show. The recording is mainly filmed in close-ups and mediums. A head is sometimes visible in the wide shots of the musical numbers. Recording includes the curtain call and marquee.

Exceptional close-up video from the first few rows of the Daryl Roth. Filmed in 4k vertical and edited in 3:2 1080p. This was the Tistanique fan night performance, so the crowd is rabid, and the cast members are completely unhinged. So many amazing new adlibs (especially from Drew, who made almost every person on stage break at one point). The improv section is all about Constantine and Marla's (writers of the show) journey to get it to stage, and a lot of other jokes at their expense (to their immense delight). Lots of laughter and raucous applause from the audience. Includes all the after-show shenanigans including trivia, a drawing contest, and a lip-sync turned strip show. A wild night was had by all. Definitely can't recommend this show enough. It's shiploads of fun.
